extracted.intended_audience: United States Indian Agents, Commissioner of Indian Affairs, and Department administrators
extracted.subtask_description: Extracted criteria and standards used in 1880 annual reports by U.S. Indian agents concerning reservation administration, education, supplies distribution, and civilizing policies. Focuses on operational recommendations, schooling and industrial-training practices, logistics, and policy suggestions for agents and the Department.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education as primary avenue to civilization
rubrics_metrics.description: The shortest road in the civilization of the Indian is through the education of the youth; education builds the bridge on which the Indian passes to civilization and that better life of Christian love and happiness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agents should prioritize schooling (day and boarding/manual labor schools), supply teachers, encourage attendance, and expand facilities. Education is presented as the chief means to effect moral and social change.

rubrics_metrics.name: School capacity must meet demand
rubrics_metrics.description: Report lists number of children of school-going age versus number accommodated (e.g., number of children of school-going age is 438; number who can be accommodated, 277; number of schools, 4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agents must record enrollment and capacity, highlight shortages, and request building appropriations when capacity is insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of food/rations as attendance incentive
rubrics_metrics.description: In day schools a lunch or ration is issued to each scholar attending a full day as an inducement to those who are poor and not inclined to accept education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This plan is effective: small expenditure returns interest by increasing attendance and stimulating parental encouragement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective word method for language instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: Instruction is objective; language mastery is the first point. Use the objective-word method: present object or thought first, then the language to express it. Begin with script characters, teach reading and writing together using blackboard and drill in elementary sounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beginners use no text-books; specific recommended materials include Webb's Model First Reader, Appleton's Second, Keep's Stories, Grube's method for numbers, and Picture-Teaching where affordable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial and trade instruction organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Industrial instruction organized into trades (blacksmith, wagon-maker, carpenter, harness-maker, tinner, shoemaker, tailor, printing, baking, farming) with apprentices; apprentices remain in a chosen trade except for extraordinary reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schedule: trades work a day and a half or two days each week and attend school remaining days; maintain night-school for older youths; provide competent practical workmen as instructors. Track outputs (e.g., harnesses, tinware, shoes) as measures of practical success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation of children from parental homes to aid reform
rubrics_metrics.description: The results justify the wisdom of a complete separation of Indian children from their parents and the debasing influences of their homes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argues for boarding/manual labor schools and institutional separation as a deliberate policy to accelerate 'civilization'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work requirement for able-bodied men receiving aid
rubrics_metrics.description: Carrying out provisions of the act of Congress in 1875: require every able-bodied male Indian to work for what he receives from the government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy enforced at agency level; seen as wholesome and effective in promoting sobriety and industry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt issuance of patents to allotments
rubrics_metrics.description: Necessity of issuing patents to those to whom allotments have been made, as an act of justice; long waiting retards work and discourages Indians from investing labor (fear of having improvements taken).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issuing patents will assure the Indian that he cannot be disturbed in his rights and will encourage settlement and development of cleared farms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depot locations and transport modes for delivery of goods
rubrics_metrics.description: Goods and supplies are deposited at Bayfield for certain reservations and at Duluth for others; delivery uses steamboat/tug, railroad, and teams depending on reservation. Examples: steamer to cross lake for Grand Portage; railroad to Chandler then teams for Lac Court d'Oreille.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agents must plan deliveries according to geography and available transport; note costs (e.g., $150–$200 to reach Grand Portage by tug) and practical constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feasibility of using Indian teams for hauling depends on roads and distance
rubrics_metrics.description: The wagons and oxen furnished cannot be used for transporting supplies now because agency location, reservation distances, and poor roads make the task impracticable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend improving roads and building bridges (e.g., fix road between Ashland and Bad River, repair winter road used) before expecting Indians to haul supplies; where roads are fixed, use of Indian teams may be feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set aside and survey land for agricultural/educational use
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommend setting aside 1,000 acres on south side of Vermillion Lake for agricultural and educational purposes, defining boundaries by survey and inducing Indians to select homes and settle thereon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Land reservation for farming and schooling is proposed to create a stable settlement and productive demonstration area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide farmers and agricultural instruction to tribes
rubrics_metrics.description: With a farmer to show them the way, their advancement would be as rapid as those in any other section; farmers and assistants are employed and needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agents should station a farmer and assistant farmer at agencies/reservations to instruct in planting, saving seed, and farming practices; supply seed in time for sowing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide livestock, implements, and fencing to support farming
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for breeding mares, a stallion, sheep, agricultural implements (reapers, mowers), and barbed wire to prevent burning fences and to fence meadow land to secure forage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issue stock to those advanced in farming; provide implements and fencing to enable hay production and protect equipment; estimate and request supplies in annuity goods budgets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annuity disbursement per treaty and departmental instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Bois Forte annuity broken down by categories (money per capita, educational, farming, blacksmith/support, provisions/ammunition/tobacco, goods), with agent disbursing certain funds and department purchasing and furnishing goods to agent for distribution according to instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agents must adhere to department instructions in distribution and keep account of disbursements; note specific sums and allocations in reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommend small police forces where beneficial
rubrics_metrics.description: No police force existed at the agency during the past year; a small force on Red Cliff and Bad River Reservations would be advantageous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department authorization for reservation police is recommended to maintain order and enforce regulations locally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respond to disasters with emergency seed and relief
rubrics_metrics.description: Floods and fires devastated crops and homes, leaving Indians without seed and subsistence; department will likely need to furnish seed the next year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agents should document crop failures and disasters and request emergency seed and supplies; anticipate the need to supply seed even if it was hoped unnecessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure school success by academic progress and industrial output
rubrics_metrics.description: Progress judged by advancement in reading, arithmetic, writing, correspondence with parents, and industrial products (e.g., number of harness sets, tinware produced, pairs of shoes repaired).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports should include both academic performance indicators and concrete measures from shops and farm to demonstrate practical success and justify appropriations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection, retention, and return of pupils based on fitness and agency needs
rubrics_metrics.description: Some older or more advanced pupils were returned to agencies as workers or for being heads of families; others returned for imperfect physical or mental condition or at chiefs' request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schools should track pupil fitness, age, maturity, and agency needs; retention decisions should balance training goals with community and family circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use exhibits and public display to validate school work
rubrics_metrics.description: Exhibitions (e.g., fall fair) displayed work of all departments and attracted favorable comment; a committee examined and reported on the exhibit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use public exhibitions and third-party review to validate and publicize school accomplishments and secure support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issue tools/vehicles to worthy Indians as incentives and training aids
rubrics_metrics.description: Fifty wagons furnished by the department were issued to worthy Indians; recipients prized them, built sheds for protection, and learned care and industry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select deserving individuals for resource issuance to encourage responsibility and model behavior; small investments can have emulative effects.
